definition_english: Characterizing a vascular plant—either woody or herbaceous dying back above ground during unfavorable seasons and regenerating from persistent roots or storage organs—that lives and reproduces across three or more annual growing cycles; as a countable noun, a plant of this life-cycle type.
definition_hindi: तीन या अधिक वार्षिक वृद्धि चक्रों तक जीवित रहने और प्रजनन करने वाले संवहनी पादप (काष्ठीय अथवा शाकीय, जो प्रतिकूल ऋतुओं में भूमि के ऊपर सूखकर भूमिगत जड़ों या संचयी अंगों से पुनः उगते हैं) का विशेषण; गणनीय संज्ञा के रूप में इस जीवन-चक्र प्रकार का पौधा।

hindi_equivalents_etymology.बारहमासी: Native Hindi compound बारह + मास (bārah + mās, 'twelve + months'), attested in Hindi Shabdasagar Part 5, p. 147
hindi_equivalents_etymology.सदाबहार: Compound combining Sanskrit सदा (sadā) and Persian बहार (bahār)
hindi_equivalents_etymology.परेनीअल: Devanagari phonetic transliteration of English perennial (attested in Shabdkosh)

register_and_pragmatics.academic_register: Technical botanical and agricultural register (बहुवर्षी / बहुवर्षीय); general textbook and horticultural register (बारहमासी)
register_and_pragmatics.connotation: Neutral in scientific usage (बहुवर्षी); mildly positive/abundant in everyday usage (बारहमासी, सदाबहार)
cultural_nuances: Hindi lacks a compact single-word countable noun matching English 'perennials' in academic prose, requiring expansion into noun phrases such as बहुवर्षी पादप or बारहमासी पौधे.
बारहमासी bridges colloquial gardening, classical Hindi literature (Hindi Shabdasagar), and institutional publications (CSTT PDF, eGyanKosh).
usage_restrictions: Avoid equating perennial with सदाबहार (evergreen) in botany, as deciduous perennials shed foliage seasonally while surviving underground.
Do not confuse the botanical adjective/flower name बारहमासी with the masculine poetic genre noun बारहमासा (bārahmāsā).
Avoid phonetic transliteration परेनीअल in formal academic or scientific Hindi.

linguistic_analysis.morphosyntax: English perennial functions both as an attributive/predicative adjective and as a countable noun taking plural -s (perennials). Hindi बहुवर्षी, बहुवर्षीय, and बारहमासी are morphologically invariable adjectives (अविकारी विशेषण) that do not inflect for gender, number, or case; inflection and postpositions attach to the modified head noun (e.g., बारहमासी फलों में, बारहमासी पौधे).
linguistic_analysis.translation_asymmetry: Translating the English countable plural noun 'perennials' requires syntactic expansion into a Hindi noun phrase (बहुवर्षी पादप or बारहमासी पौधे) because Hindi lacks a standalone one-word botanical noun.

conceptual_analysis.core_distinction: Defines biological longevity across three or more annual growing cycles, encompassing both woody trees/shrubs and herbaceous plants that die back above ground during unfavorable seasons and regenerate from persistent roots or storage organs.
conceptual_analysis.domain_boundary: Strictly restricted to botanical and horticultural life-cycle classification (S1); distinct from year-round water flow in hydrology (S2), persistent socio-historical issues (S3), permanent departmental staffing (S4), and timeless philosophical doctrines (S5).

pairwise_comparison.semantic_overlap: Both denote multi-year plant survival beyond annual and biennial life cycles.
pairwise_comparison.difference: बहुवर्षी / बहुवर्षीय explicitly denotes living three or more years (covering herbaceous perennials with winter die-back), whereas बारहमासी literally means 'twelve-monthly' (flowering/fruiting across all twelve months) and can also denote a specific five-petaled garden flower.
pairwise_comparison.interchangeability: High in general horticulture and introductory science; prefer बहुवर्षी / बहुवर्षीय in strict botanical taxonomy and plant physiology.

pairwise_comparison.semantic_overlap: Minimal; linked primarily through bilingual dictionary listings (such as Shabdkosh's सदाबहार वृक्ष) that conflate multi-year survival with year-round foliage.
pairwise_comparison.difference: बहुवर्षी refers to multi-year life-cycle duration (including deciduous plants), whereas सदाबहार denotes continuous green foliage without seasonal leaf-shedding (evergreen).
pairwise_comparison.interchangeability: Not interchangeable in botany; using सदाबहार for deciduous perennials is a conceptual error.

pairwise_comparison.semantic_overlap: Both appear in classical Hindi dictionaries (Hindwi, Hindi Shabdasagar) for plants bearing fruit or flowers continuously across seasons.
pairwise_comparison.difference: बारहमासी is actively attested in modern institutional texts (CSTT PDF, eGyanKosh) and general horticulture, whereas सदाफल is an archaic/literary dictionary synonym.
pairwise_comparison.interchangeability: Low; prefer बारहमासी or बहुवर्षी in modern academic prose.

proposed_terminology.justification: Existing Hindi terms बहुवर्षी / बहुवर्षीय (for strict botanical longevity) and बारहमासी (for general horticultural and textbook usage) are already attested and semantically adequate; no new coinage is needed.

overall_confidence: Moderate-High — Botanical sense S1 and Hindi equivalents बहुवर्षी, बहुवर्षीय, and बारहमासी are well-attested across Hindwi, Hindi Shabdasagar, eGyanKosh, and CSTT prose, though an explicit CSTT English-Hindi headword record for perennial remains unverified.
